# Exp 1 / R4: profit-model fidelity vs AC-OPF (generated by experiments/exp1_fidelity.py)

- Test set: 200 states (episodes) x 5 scenarios = 1000 scenarios x markups [1.0, 1.2, 1.5, 2.0, 2.5, 3.0]; events per state: {'thunderstorm': 40, 'gas_price': 70, 'none': 27, 'planned_outage': 50, 'heatwave': 42}; outages: {'38-37': 12, '65-68': 13, '49-54#1': 3, '15-33': 6, '49-66#1': 2, '49-66#2': 5, '56-57': 6, '49-54#2': 3}; in-distribution scenarios 436/1000; scenarios with AC scarcity (LMP >= 500) at some markup: 29.
- AC status counts: {'LOCALLY_SOLVED': 6000}.
- Hardware: CPU Intel(R) Xeon(R) Gold 6448Y, GPU NVIDIA A100-SXM4-80GB. AC / DC-IPOPT / DC-HiGHS(pool) use the 16-worker CPU solver pool (1 thread each); DC-HiGHS-1core runs in-process on one core; GENCO runs on one A100 (shared node) + 1 CPU core, all 6 markups of all scenarios in one batch. GENCO+dc_hybrid cost includes the 1-core DC LP.
- cost_s = wall s per (scenario, markup) over the whole test set; n50 = same for an agent-sized call (50 scenarios x 6 markups). rho_within = correlation after removing each state's mean (what the multi-fidelity estimator inside one decision sees); MF x = 1 / variance ratio of README result 3 with rho_within and r = c_AC / c_model.
